sections.html:
Groveland sits in southwest Lake County, where State Road 50, State Road 19 and State Road 33 meet. It is 27 miles west of downtown Orlando, 35 miles from Walt Disney World and 70 miles from Tampa, so commuters heading toward Orlando or Clermont are natural buyers.

The city counts more than 26,800 residents, and many recent arrivals came from the Orlando area. Builders, investors and families all shop here at once, which means a Groveland owner can usually compare several kinds of buyer before picking a way to sell.

The City of Groveland Building Division handles residential and commercial permits and checks plans against the Florida Building Code. If you had a roof, windows, an addition or a shed done, ask the division whether each job has a closed permit before a buyer's inspector asks the same thing.

The same office registers building contractors, issues Certificates of Occupancy for new homes and holds the permit and inspection files. Its office is at 6825 SR 50, second floor. Call 352-429-2141, option 2, or write to permitting@groveland-fl.gov. The counter is open Monday to Thursday from 8 to 5, and Friday from 8 to 3 with remote service until 5. Inspections are scheduled through the city's eTrakit portal, and fire inspections go through the Fire Inspector at 352-467-0493.

  • Request the permit record for your parcel early.
  • Ask how to close any permit that never got a final inspection.
  • Gather contractor invoices that show permit numbers.

sections.h2: When do Lake County property taxes come due?
sections.html:
The Lake County Tax Collector starts collecting each November 1 for the January to December tax year. The bill goes to the owner's address on the tax roll. If a mortgage company pays through escrow, an escrow code prints on the notice, and the owner still gets a copy.

Early-payment discounts, Lake County Tax Collector

November 304%

Taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and 3% statutory interest is added at that point. A mailed check counts as paid on its postmark date. To change the name, mailing address or assessed value on the roll, call the Lake County Property Appraiser at 352-253-2150, because the tax collector cannot make those changes.

Lake County's homestead exemption lowers assessed value by up to $51,411. Owners who lived in the home on January 1 file by March 1. Approval letters are not mailed, and once approved it carries forward every year until the house is used differently.

  • Widow or widower: $5,000 off assessed value, ended by remarriage.
  • Disability: $5,000 with a physician statement on Form DR-416 or a Social Security letter.
  • Limited income senior: up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older, with a household income cap of $38,686. Lake County and Minneola authorize the full amount, and Clermont, Lady Lake, Mount Dora and Tavares authorize up to $25,000. Ask the appraiser what applies to a Groveland parcel.
  • Military and deployed service members: separate exemptions, each with a March 1 deadline.

When the house sells, the Save Our Homes cap starts over, and the next owner is first assessed at just value. Renting out the house or moving away ends a homestead.

Honorably discharged service members rated 10 percent or more can take a $5,000 reduction, proven by a VA letter. A homestead can be fully exempt for a person rated totally and permanently disabled, and for some surviving spouses. A buyer in that group who closes early in the year may also qualify for a pro-rated first-year refund, which the tax collector starts after the following bill is paid.

Two more full exemptions cover the unremarried spouse of a first responder killed on duty and a first responder permanently disabled on duty. Each needs paperwork, so call 352-253-2150 if someone in your deal might qualify.

The deed carries Florida documentary stamp tax under section 201.02. The Lake County clerk collects it along with recording charges when the deed is filed. The final charge shifts with page count and the names on the deed, so get a figure from the clerk or the closing agent before you sign.

sections.h2: What proof can you give a buyer's lender?
sections.html:
Lake County's appraiser does not write letters confirming a homestead. All exemption data is public, so owners print or save the property record card, where green checkmarks mark each exemption granted, and send that to the servicer. The card also shows a working tax estimate. The official figure is the proposed-tax notice mailed in mid-August.

  • Trust ownership: the applicant needs equitable title or a beneficial interest, and the appraiser can ask for the trust agreement.
  • Contract for deed: eligible only if the contract is recorded with the Clerk of the Court and a copy reaches the appraiser. An ordinary purchase contract does not count.
  • A move within Lake County: homestead does not transfer by itself, so the new address needs a new application.

A delinquent house is a separate problem. If an investor buys a certificate on an unpaid year, that investor may apply for a deed two years later. Pay off any old year first: the tax collector can quote the balance and your closing agent can send it from the sale proceeds.

Start with the paperwork you control. Pull the permit record, print the property record card, and get the current tax figure from the Lake County Tax Collector. Then collect written terms from each buyer and compare the net amount, not the headline price.

After the contract is signed, the closing agent orders title work and requests a payoff letter for each loan, then drafts the deed. The county clerk records it and takes the stamp tax. Any property tax still open for the year is divided between you and the buyer at the table. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, which removes one common reason for a delay, but title work and recording still take time. Get the timeline in writing before committing to a day.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Groveland house
sections.html:
• Agent listing: public showings and a negotiation after the inspection.
  • Sale by owner: you manage the contract, disclosures and recording yourself.
  • Cash purchase: the price reflects the house as it sits, and the two sides agree on a closing day.

From each buyer, get terms in writing, the exact net amount and the day the money lands. Gather the permit history, the tax bill and any tenant details before offers arrive, and the comparison gets simpler. A folder holding the deed, the latest tax notice, the property record card and permit numbers can save days after a contract is signed.

faqs.q: Does Groveland have its own building department?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Division at 352-429-2141, option 2, keeps permit records and schedules inspections.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Collection starts November 1. The best discount is 4% through November 30, and the gross amount is due by March 31.

faqs.q: Is there a Groveland homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Lake County gives up to $51,411 off assessed value for a permanent residence, with applications due March 1. Approved exemptions renew themselves.

faqs.q: Is there a state tax on a Groveland deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 201.02 taxes the deed, and the clerk takes payment at recording, usually through your closing agent.

faqs.q: Must I fix a Groveland house first?
faqs.a: No, some buyers purchase in present condition. Open permits deserve a call to the Building Division before you sign.
